title: The Council meets
caption: This is not a courtesy. The Constitution requires the President to hold regular meetings with the Vice-President and all the Ministers, and this ring of table is where they are held.

check.question: Whom must the President meet with regularly?
options: The leadership of the National Assembly
The Vice-President and all the Ministers
check.explain: The President is required to hold regular meetings with the Vice-President and all the Ministers of the Government of the Federation. That body is what is called the Federal Executive Council.

title: The head of the table
caption: One place is unlike the rest. The executive powers of the Federation are vested in the President — in one person, not in the table — who may use them directly or through the Vice-President, the Ministers and the public service.

check.question: In whom does the Constitution vest the executive powers of the Federation?
check.explain: They are vested in the President, who may exercise them directly or through the Vice-President, Ministers and officers of the public service.

title: A minister from every state
caption: The table is this long for a reason. A minister is appointed by the President once the Senate has confirmed the nomination, and the President must appoint at least one from each state, who must be an indigene of it.

check.question: Could a President choose every minister from just a handful of states?
options: Yes — ministers are the President's choice alone
No — each state must have at least one
check.explain: The President must appoint at least one minister from each state, and that minister must be an indigene of the state. Every nomination also has to be confirmed by the Senate.

title: A minister speaks
caption: A minister puts something before the table. The Constitution names what these meetings are for: settling the general direction of domestic and foreign policy, and co-ordinating what the President, the Vice-President and the Ministers each do.

title: Advice, to one person
caption: The third purpose the Constitution gives the meeting is to advise the President generally on the discharge of the office's executive functions. The table advises and the office at its head decides, because that is where the power is vested.

title: The one thing it can do alone
caption: There is a single decision that belongs to this table and not to its head. If two-thirds of all its members resolve that the President or Vice-President is incapable of discharging the functions of the office, a medical panel is asked to verify it.

check.question: The Council believes the President can no longer do the job. What does it take to declare so?
options: A simple majority of those present
check.explain: It takes a resolution passed by a two-thirds majority of all the members of the executive council. The declaration then has to be verified by a medical panel before the President ceases to hold office.
